verdicts.claim: SQLite auto-checkpoints when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, and when the last connection closes.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages" ... "or when the last database connection on a database file closes."

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints and sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() use PASSIVE mode.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE." (c1-2 page does not state it)

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and never invokes the busy handler.
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: "Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish"; "The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode."

verdicts.claim: FULL waits for no active writer and all readers on the latest snapshot.
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2 FULL: "This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer" and all readers are reading from the most recent snapshot; fetch summary confirmed the writer half verbatim.

verdicts.claim: RESTART also waits until readers use only the database file.
verdicts.evidence: RESTART: "it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback) until all readers are reading from the database file only."

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE is RESTART plus truncating the WAL to zero bytes; a successful TRUNCATE reports pnLog and pnCkpt as 0.
verdicts.evidence: TRUNCATE: "it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return"; after success "both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero."

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint normally does not shrink the WAL file; it restarts overwriting from the start; truncated only when journal_size_limit set
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning."

verdicts.claim: If a reader always overlaps, no checkpoint completes and the WAL grows without bound (checkpoint starvation).
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound."

verdicts.claim: Mitigations for starvation: schedule manual RESTART or TRUNCATE checkpoints in reader gaps, keep read transactions short, and finalize or reset statements.
verdicts.evidence: Partial: wal.html supports 'reader gaps' and forcing completion; neither cited page mentions finalizing/resetting statements or explicitly keeping read transactions short, and a WebSearch found no primary source for the finalize/reset advice.

verdicts.claim: A rare WAL-reset bug affecting 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 was fixed in 3.51.3.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later."

notes: Source cache returned provenance-only hits (no text path) for all three URLs; 3 WebFetch + 1 WebSearch used.
